originality.rationale: Eliseev's Proposition 2 proof already tracks every Gram entry modulo \(p^2\) under the same mutation, sign-change, and isometry operations. Because the mutation coefficient is divisible by \(p\), the correction terms are \(0\pmod{p^2}\), the mutated adjacent entry is the negative of the old one, sign changes multiply the corresponding row/column by \(-1\), and isometries leave the Gram matrix fixed. Dividing the skew part by \(p\) therefore gives exactly the assigned signed-permutation covariance. The triangle-square multiset is then the standard elementary invariant of such a signed switching action. Thus the claim is a useful repackaging, but mechanically implied by the inspected primary proof.
